source.semantics: RequestResetPasswordAsync clears prior message/error state, requires a selected application user, validates that the new password is present and exactly matches its confirmation, then opens the reset confirmation dialog. It does not mutate credentials; ConfirmResetPasswordAsync owns the later reset mutation.

laravel_adaptation.semantics: The existing tenant-scoped Application Users password-reset workspace now preserves the source two-step boundary. Review reset carries this canonical operation ID, validates selected user plus required/matching password fields, and opens a review/confirmation state without POSTing. Only a second explicit confirmation can invoke the already-existing password reset mutation.

security_invariants: The request/review operation performs no server, WordPress, connector, queue, cache, credential, session or audit mutation.
The reset workspace remains hidden unless the authenticated active-tenant context grants members.manage and supplies the tenant-derived application-users endpoint.
No tenant, user or membership identity is accepted by the request control itself; the selected membership comes only from the authoritative tenant-scoped member list.

The existing mutation operation remains distinct and continues to enforce server-side tenant membership resolution, confirmation identity, CSRF, password policy, session revocation, audit and authoritative reread.
failure_behavior: Missing selection, missing password or mismatched confirmation does not open review and cannot send the reset mutation. Review can be cancelled locally. Duplicate mutation remains blocked while the existing reset mutation is pending.
no_duplicate_work: This closure does not reimplement password persistence. It adds only the missing source-equivalent RequestResetPasswordAsync review gate and leaves AIMW-BILL-3BE40F2E00 as the sole credential mutation operation.
